newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine shares fall as blue chips tumble.
newsitem.headline: Philippine shares fall as blue chips tumble.

text.p: The Philippine share index fell sharply by midsession as board-based selling swept across blue chips following a speculative attack on the peso, brokers said.
Edser Trinidad, analyst at Peregrine Securities, said market sentiment was easily swayed to the negative side when a fresh wave of speculative selling hit the peso.
"The market has been listless in the past days, and here comes the Thai baht problem again ... " Trinidad said.
The main index lost 1.85 percent to 2,763.59 after an hour of trading.
In recent months, Philippine financial markets have regularly fallen victim to the troubles spilling over from the Thai baht.
The Philippines has been tagged as the next Thailand due to its structural similarities, which many local officials and analysts have downplayed.

Among the heavy losers were Ayala Corp B which shed one peso to 18 pesos, Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co Inc which lost five pesos to 565 pesos, and Ayala Land B which slipped 50 centavos to 24.00 pesos.
Joey Cuyegkeng, economist of ING Barings, said he expected shares to remain weak, but added the situation would provide the opportunity to buy into the market.
